utterances.text: Lastly, can you tell the Trial Chamber how it was that you succeeded in taking Kunjerac and at what -- at which point did this take place?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We succeeded in doing so when we torched two houses with a Zolja. It was at that point that the Serbs withdrew in the direction of Sase.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why did you set these two houses on fire with Zoljas? Can you tell the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was from those houses that the fiercest resistance was coming from. There was an anti-aircraft gun placed in one of the houses which was constantly firing upon us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were these the same houses that you said had machine-gun emplacements in them?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those were the houses that were well-fortified with sandbags and where machine-gun nests were placed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Again, no interruption. Perhaps I missed something, but I can't see Kunjerac on this -- on D964 and I wonder if it might -- I don't know if it's indicated, first of all, and if isn't, the witness may be able to tell us where it is. It makes it a little easier to follow this evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I thank you, Mr. Di Fazio. Perhaps the witness can deal with that easily I suppose?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I was just about to ask the witness to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber what Kunjerac is and then point it to us on the map if it's there; if not, just show its location.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kunjerac is a hill above Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please point it on the map for the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record -- one moment, let me register that. For the record, the witness indicates with a line to the right of Biljaca the area which he claims to be Kunjerac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you please mark it with a "K," but before you do that could I ask you the following: The Kunjerac hill, in your opinion, how far apart is it from the centre of Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean as the crow flies or --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As the crow flies, please.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some 500 to 700 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is Kunjerac in fact part of Bjelovac, the locality of Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's right above Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is there any important facility at Kunjerac as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a water reservoir there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What you were able to observe at Kunjerac during the fighting, could you observe who you were fighting against? Were those village guards?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we climbed up to Kunjerac, we found 72-, 120-, and 62-millimetre mortars there. I already indicated there was a anti-aircraft gun, there were two machine-guns, several other machine-guns, and a large quantity of side arms. There were anti-armoured weapons, OSA, and the hand-held rocket launcher, 50-calibre.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you fighting units there or were you fighting villagers who were not in uniforms?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Kunjerac we fought against several units.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber which units these were?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we were taking Kunjerac, we collected weapons and ammunition from soldiers who perished. We also took their clothes and footwear. And based on their IDs and the patches they wore on their sleeves, we were able to conclude that several units had taken part in the clashes. One of them was the Krajina Battalion, another was the Bratunac Brigade, Mungos's unit, Kokara's unit, and the Red Berets, volunteers from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could it have the usher's assistance in showing the witness a new Defence exhibit. This is the list of soldiers of the military post 2465/5 who were paid their travel allowance and salaries for October 1992. The document bears the number 01319806.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, Witness, please could you turn to the last page of this document where the following title is contained: Special-purpose unit (Mungos)." Please take a look at the list there and look at the person under 375, Milenko Prodanovic, did you know this person from before the war?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. He was a bus conductor for the Vihor company in Bratunac, where in mid-1990, he, as a volunteer with another group of Serbs from Bratunac, went to the front line in Croatia. From conversations I had in the field as a police officer, I found out that he had committed grave crimes against the Catholics over there. In May 1992 when the villages of Voljavica, Zaluzje, and others were -- the Muslim villages were cleansed, he was there with his group and other local Serbs. The people from the area were able to recognise him, and they afterwards fled to Srebrenica and were at my place.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he have a nickname of a sorts?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mungos.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could this document be assigned a Defence exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for His Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So this document which consists of three pages in B/C/S and three pages in English with the following ERN numbers: 0 -- the first page is handwritten and it has the following ERN: 01319805. The second and the third are typed or printed pages, and they have respectively the following ERNs: 01319806 and 01319816. The three pages in English are corresponding translation of the B/C/S, and they show the same ERN numbers. This document is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D973.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the clashes that took place for Kunjerac, did there come a time that you learnt about Mungos's presence there?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was on the second day of fighting that the Serbs who were at Kunjerac called Mungos by his name. And they said, "Mungos come out of the forest. Kokara, why don't you approach them from the left flank." They threatened that Mungos and Kokara would kill us all.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were able to discern that from what individual Serbs were yelling amongst each other?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because we were very close to their lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wish to also draw upon Defence Exhibit D271, which is a video, which is the Serb radio communication where the names of Kokara and Mungos are mentioned. We already had occasion to listen to that. I don't wish to re-introduce it here, I just wish to invoke it here again, together with a transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Okay. Thank you. I don't think there is a need to put it to the witness because he can listen or hear what we can. Let's move ahead. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You've also indicated that you saw the patches that the Serb soldiers wore on their sleeves. You mentioned a volunteers' unit from Serbia. Which unit was that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Likewise, you mentioned people from a different part of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from Krajina, the Krajina Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown D257 now. This is a record sheet for a dead fighter dated 29 September 1993. I will quote -- according to this record sheet, does the name of the following persons: "Zeljko Knezevic, son of Vojislav, date and place of birth, 30 December 1966. Pecenog Ilova, date and place of death, 16 December 1992, Kunjerac. How the death occurred, in combat. Unit: Krajina Battalion."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does this document reflect accurately the situation in terms of the participation of the Krajina Battalion in the fighting at Kunjerac on the 16th December?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown Prosecution Exhibit P589. This is an article published in the Dnevni telegraph on the 16th of December 1997. Bearing the number 0296320 entitled: "Top was not in the Red Berets."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that you've read the article?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will quote just a small part which is the -- Dejan Jevtic's statement. He was commander of special units at the Eastern Bosnian battlefield. He says: "I personally commanded the actions around Visegrad, Srebrenica, Bratunac, Gorazde, Cajnice, and Foca." My question to you is as follows: To your knowledge is it true that the Red Berets operated in the area of Srebrenica and Bratunac in the course of 1992, including the fighting in the general area of Bjelovac that you've just described?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't need the document anymore. Thank you. I want to turn to a different topic now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that during the fighting there you were on the Kunjerac hill, and I understood you to mean that the battle lasted two days. From that vantage point were you able to see what was happening in Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which area could be seen from your vantage point?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area from Bjelovac to Loznicka Rijeka, but that means only a part of Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to observe Serb positions -- first of all, were there any Serb positions in the area?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was able to observe artillery positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And how were you able to see the positions?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had two hunting binoculars in my group, and we used them to observe the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned artillery pieces. Do you know which artillery pieces were involved?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, these were 105- and 155-millimetre Howitzers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber where they were positioned?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The artillery positions were located in the valley below Bjelovac toward the Drina River.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you or were you not able to see any armoured vehicles?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a tank there which was dug-in with the tube or barrel facing the villages of Pirici, Jovanovici. The tank was active on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to see any APCs?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, two APCs which went along the route Bjelovac to Loznicka Rijeka. They moved to and fro, opening fire in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would like you to take a look at a Defence exhibit now. This is a document by the Bratunac Brigade dated 29 July 1994, bearing the following number: 04364833. The title being: "Information regarding tanks and armoured personnel carriers to be delivered to the Drina Corps command." Witness, do you have the document before you?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see item 1 and the fact that it contains the tanks and APCs that the Serb army had at the beginning of the war?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In item 2 it is stated as follows: "Since the start of the war the following have been destroyed in combat: T-55 tank, one (Bjelovac); armoured APCs, M-60, two (Zaluzje)." Are you aware of the presence of these tanks and do you know how they came to be destroyed?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A while ago I said that as I was visiting in the hospital --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, I would like you to be fully understood by the Trial Chamber. It was in the final stages of the battle that you were wounded, is it not?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I just want to make sure that the Chamber can follow. When did you learn about the existence of these tanks, about this fact?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the hospital when I found this out from members of Zaka's group who were from the area of Voljavica, and they came to visit me there. They told me that as they were entering Bjelovac they came across destroyed -- a destroyed tank and destroyed APCs which the Serbs had destroyed as they had been withdrawing. They also told me that as they entered Sase they came across a T-34 tank, which was disabled because the primer was taken from the tank, disabling it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Alic's group. Was it the group from Srebrenica or from the area of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, from the municipality of Bratunac, from Voljavica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this document be assigned a number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic. This document, which consists of two pages, one being a translation in English of the other, which is in B/C/S, and has -- bears ERN number 04364833 is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D974.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The fighting you described, which took place between the 14th and the 16th of December 1992, based on what you saw, did the fighting take place in the centre of Bjelovac or elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fiercest battles took place at the entrance to Loznicka Rijeka because it was there that the Serb army had its strongholds.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where the Serb strongholds were located?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were located in between and next to the houses in Loznicka Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "strongholds," what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very strong military positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you describe that for the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. These are positions which are well-equipped with units, weaponry, and pieces, artillery pieces.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that these strongholds were in front of the houses there and in between the houses. How were you able to know this?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know this because I was told that by the people who came to visit me in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You mentioned planes, saying that they flew over the entire area. Were you under the impression or were you able to conclude that they had specific targets which they were aiming after or were they targeting undiscriminately?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were targeting Loznicka Rijeka because they believed that that was where our fighters were located and the general area of Loznicka Rijeka toward Jovanovici. The bombardments resulted in the deaths of many of our fighters and in the deaths of many Serb civilians who were in the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly that it was through their fault?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was through their own fault that they targeted those people, just as they had erroneously dropped ammunition in our hands.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In these fightings around Kunjerac and in the area of Bjelovac, did -- were you able to see Naser Oric at any point?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Of these groups, who was with you at Kunjerac?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Midhat Salihovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At some point you told us that you were wounded in the fighting at Kunjerac. Can you briefly describe for the Trial Chamber the circumstances under which you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This took place on the 16th when the fighting was drawing to a close, we noticed that there was a machine-gun emplacement in a barn. As the fighting subsided, a large group of people ran out of the woods there in the direction of the barn because they believed that there was food there. I was only able to run out of my shelter to push the people back from where they were going, and it was at that point that I felt this blow on my head. I dropped down on the ground, and when I came to I noticed that there were dozens of dead people lying around me. The person manning the machine-gun managed to wound me and kill those other people.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you were basically wounded in an attempt to push the Muslim civilians away from the area?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were Muslim civilians there who came there with the intention of finding food.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours again -- not an objection, but I don't -- I think a clarification. A question was asked -- well, several questions - about who was present with this witness in -- at Kunjerac. And Madam Vidovic asked whether Mr. Oric was visible. The witness said "no." Then she asked: "Of these groups," of these groups, plural, "who was with you at Kunjerac?" Perhaps I misunderstood the earlier evidence, but I don't recall there being any evidence of other groups in the area than what this witness has spoken. Of course, as you know, from the Prosecution's point of view it's important to know which groups. And is the witness confining himself purely and simply to the hill of Kunjerac, or were there other groups in the wider area around Bjelovac? And that's left unclear, in my submission, unless I missed something from earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we can refer it straight to the witness. Did -- Mr. Smajlovic, have you been able to follow what Mr. Di Fazio has pointed out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you clarify matters further? Can you give a better, perhaps, description of what you have already stated, which would explain to Mr. Di Fazio what is doubtful in his mind or is not clear in his mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. At Kunjerac there was only Midhat Salihovic's group as well as mine, but in the greater area, as I've mentioned before, there were Zaka's men. His group was in Voljavica, and they came to see me in the hospital. That is the greater area of that territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it's clear. I mean, that's how I understood it in the first place, but anyway let's move forward, please, thank you. You're satisfied, I take it, Mr. Di Fazio?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, and if I missed it, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, it happens. Everyone gets tired after a certain -- I am feeling tired, myself, today. Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, sorry, just one matter which has come up in the meantime concerning this witness who is to be here next week. As I understand it the government in question was cancelling his travel. The Victims and Witnesses Unit is trying to re-instate it. I think probably we need an indication that he should travel, and I need to say that the US government isn't -- has expressed its dissatisfaction or its unhappiness with us, unfortunately, but we're endeavouring to explain the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It never rains but pours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, then perhaps I should excuse myself from court for ten minutes and perhaps I can --.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I -- certainly you have our permission for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I think you can convey to the US government our conviction that you can be blamed for nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Except maybe for raising the issue, but -- which you had a right to do. But otherwise ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, I'm obliged, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Yes, let's move forward, please, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you said a minute ago that you were wounded and that you were hospitalised and you were wounded as the fighting in Kunjerac was subsiding. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you the following: Did you discuss it with anyone as to what was happening in Sase?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I spoke about it with Resid. I can't recall his last name, but he is from the village of Dimnici just above Sase.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: For time constraints, could you please briefly tell us what he told you. I know he must have said a greater deal -- a great deal about the events, but could you tell us how he was wounded and something he said about the civilians.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since he was familiar with the terrain, he said that once he came down to Sase he realised that there was a pharmacy with some medication and medical equipment. He encircled the building with his group. He wanted to protect the stock found there, so as to transfer it later to Srebrenica. At the moment when they are carrying this out, a lot of people, thinking that there was food in the building, simply stampeded over him and his fighters. Although he fired warning shots, trying to tell them that there was no food there, he was unable to do anything. Lots of those civilians, baggers, entered, and they took away the medication and medical equipment. In the event he broke his arm -- or rather, the people who were pushing their way into the building broke his arm, and he was in the hospital the same time I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you quite familiar with the area of Pirici, Poloznik, and Zalazje?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As a policeman I patrolled the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the 18th of December, 1992, was it possible for a Mercedes vehicle to drive from Poloznik to Bjelovac and then through Prisoje, Biljec [phoen], Zalazje, finally reaching Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is ridiculous. From Poloznik to Bjelovac there never was a road. There was just a mountain path, and the farmers, the people used ox-carts to bring in food. There was a bridge above Sase toward Zalazje, but that one was destroyed by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. Could you tell the Chamber when the Serbs destroyed the bridge?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the 12th of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. You wanted to expand?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a road above the settlement of Vidikovac at the entrance of Srebrenica, but it was mined. So the Serbs themselves were also unable to use it in 1995, but rather they used a tunnel from Sase to reach Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in that area between the 14th and the 22nd of December, 1992, there was intensive fighting, including Sase, Kostanovice, and Andrici?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. During those days the fighting was fiercest. Lots of wounded people were brought into the hospital in that period and in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If one was to claim that he or she used a Mercedes vehicle moving through Poloznik, Bjelovac, Prisoje, Zalazje, would that be correct due to the combat activities?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because of the fighting as well as the fact that whatever vehicle appeared on the road, Bjelovac, Prisoje, and Bjelaca [phoen], was targeted from Serbia, from the Njemic feature. They could -- they used a single grenade to kill a single civilian.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction. They used shells to kill single civilians and they wouldn't waste time in destroying a vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the Serbs in January --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the Muslims in January 1993 have certain successful operations in the area of Podrinje?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything I said in the area of Kunjerac, Sase, Bjelovac, and Glogova, as well as Kravica, they were successful there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I won't go into details about such events because some other witnesses testified about that, but to ask you briefly. When it comes to the 7th of January, 1993, is it correct that you were on your way to that place and that you came to a certain point?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Ejub Golic asked for assistance; he sent a message to us. Since I was seriously wounded and my wound was swollen, I managed to reach Avdagina Njive. But I was weak, unable to move forward, and I was returned by my fighters.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore you didn't participate in what ensued?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will now move to the so-called Serb winter offensive. Did you ever hear of the Serb winter offensive?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that it was launched by mid-January 1993 in your area? What do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The refugees in the larger groups of -- in the area of Tokoljak and close to the Drina saw that strong enemy forces, including armoured and infantry units, crossed the Skelani bridge and via the hydro-electric plant at Piracac [phoen]. Among the units there were well-equipped special units as well as members of the civilian police. Those units came from the Uzice and Valjevo Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please take a look at another Defence document?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher to give another document bearing the number 04275574 to the witness. I will quote the relevant portion, that is item 2 of the document and item 3. The document is dated the 26th of January, 1993, addressed -- or rather, sent by the Uzice Corps command to the headquarters of the Army of Republika Srpska, the Drina Corps command. Item 2: "We shall keep a part of the forces of the previous artillery support at the right bank of the Drina River and we will support your forces from there, as planned and requested." Item 3: "The Uzice Corps will continue with the activities aimed at occupation of the most favourable facilities and positions." The document bears the name of Commander Major General Dragoljub Ojdanic. Witness, would you agree with me that this document confirms the information you said you received from the Muslim population of the villages in the area.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This document mentions that a part of the forces of the previous artillery support will stay at the right bank of the Drina River as support to your forces, as planned and requested. As far as you know, is it correct that as of the beginning of May 1992 until Srebrenica fell, the local Serb forces of Podrinje enjoyed artillery support from the right bank of the Drina River, that is from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I cited an example concerning Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we assign an exhibit number to the documents please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, this document, Ms. Vidovic, which consists of two pages with ERN 04273574 one in B/C/S, one in English, is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D975.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that during December 1992 you were wounded to your head, and I presume that for a certain time you did not participate in any fighting. When did you start participating in combat again and why?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the second half of January, that is the 20th of January, to be more precise, because fierce attacks ensued against the entire area of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: During those attacks that you mentioned, and during the attacks you said that came from the Army of Yugoslavia forces as well as the local population, were all the places with local Muslim population attacked?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The places that were attacked, did that group include the places which the Muslims occupied during the brief successful interval in January 1993?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did that include Bjelovac, Kravica, and its hamlets?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher to show two documents to the witness together, one being a Light Bratunac Brigade document number 04359235 dated the 4th of February, 1993, and a Light Infantry Brigade document number 04359220 dated the 7th of February, 1993, both addressed to the special brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please take first the document bearing number 04359235 dated the 4th of February, 1993. I quote: "With its main forces the special brigade shall extend the attack towards Kunjerac, while with its auxiliary forces it shall coordinate with the 1st Infantry Battalion in carrying out the mission." Please look at the second document now bearing the number 04359220. And I quote: "On the 8th of February, 1993, the special brigade with part of the forces of the 2nd Infantry Battalion shall have the task of taking and seizing defensive position on Kunjerac. It shall be supported by the brigade artillery group at the request of the commander of the special brigade." My question, hence, is the following: Is it correct that in -- at that time, on the 4th and the 7th of January [as interpreted], the Muslims were in the area of Bjelovac, Kunjerac, and Sase, that is Muslim civilians, to be more precise?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that that area was under artillery attacks by the Serb forces, as stipulated in the documents?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: During those attacks was there any damage on various buildings, houses, and all other facilities to be found in the area specified by the documents, as a result of the artillery attacks also mentioned in the documents?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They would raze everything to the ground, even if they would encounter even the slightest of resistance. They fired indiscriminately. They used tanks, guns, Howitzers, irrespective of whose house it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did they use the artillery to set houses on fire?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Using shells and incendiary ammunition, they would set houses on fire, independently of the fact to whom a given house belonged to.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we assign two exhibits to these documents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So the first one will be the document which bears ERN 04359235 consisting in one page in B/C/S and then an additional page containing the English translation thereof. This document which is dated 4th February 1993 is being marked as Defence Exhibit D976. Incidentally while -- before I mark the second one in the transcript earlier on instead of "February" we see "January." Perhaps if you find the line -- it's line 17 of previous page, page 63. That should be 7th of -- 4th and 7th of February, not of January.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The second document consists of one page with ERN 04359220 in the Serbian -- Serbo-Croat language dated 7th February 1993. The other page is the English translation thereof, and this is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D977.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I think there's a mistake in the English. It says "September," it should be "February."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I thank you for pointing that out, Mr. Di Fazio. There is definitely a mistake there. It is 7th of February and not 7th of September.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Although I find it a little strange that then this document is dated the 7th of February and then it refers to an event which took place on the 8th of February, the day after. But anyway, let's move ahead and leave these to some other point in time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is a very pertinent question, and I wish to clarify it. It states here that on the 7th of February the special brigade is tasked that during the 8th of February was to seize. That was a task for the next day, the 8th of February. We received these documents quite late from the Drina Corps archives, and I was unable to go through all of the translations, but in the Bosnian version it is quite clear that it contains a task for the next day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the next day. Okay. Thank you for making that clear, Ms. Vidovic, and we can move forward.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher to show two documents together to the witness. These are two new documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll have a break at quarter to 6.00, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. As soon as I'm finished with these two documents, and I will be brief.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, this is a Bratunac Brigade document number 04359222 dated the 7th of February, 1993, and a Bratunac Brigade document number 04359210 dated the 13th of February, 1993. The first addressed to the brigade artillery group command. Witness, please take a look at that document first with the number 04359222 dated the 7th of February addressed to the brigade artillery group command. It states: "Keep the focus of artillery support on the axis of operation of the Krajina Battalion on the Banjevici village-Kravica axis. "Readiness for action at 0700 hours." Please take a look at the other document now, dated the 13th of February, 1993, addressed to the Krajina Battalion command, specifying: "From the line of advance to the right, Gornja Brana village, trig point 574, to the left Andjici village, attack the enemy along the Gornji Bacici village, Kravica village axis with the task: Shatter and destroy the enemy on Kilavac hill and Sarampov hill on the attack axis and come out on the Krusik village, Donji Bacici village line in coordinated action with 2nd Infantry Battalion." The next sentence: "Support by a brigade artillery group and corps artillery group on request." My question concerning both of these documents is the following: To your knowledge did the Serbs in their attacks to regain the Serb villages in the Kravica area, did they use the corps artillery group as well as the brigade artillery group to attack the villages?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did their artillery cause damage on the houses in the villages of Banjevici, Kravica, Gornji and Donji Bacici, Krusik, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Various types of damage. And as I said, they destroyed everything they could and wherever they encountered any sort of resistance, irrespective of the fact whose the house was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How did you know that? Did you participate in those events?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in that area, but the people from the groups that were there told me. For example, from Midha's group, a guy called Musa was wounded and transported to Srebrenica. I went to see him since I came to their assistance before, and he told me that it was terrible there and that no one can survive from the amount -- sheer amount of shells.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we assign exhibit numbers to these documents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So the first one which consists of one page in B/C/S and one page in English, being the translation of the previous, bearing ERN 04359222 is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D978. Incidentally, with regard to this document, I'm just pointing this out to you, Madam Vidovic, maybe you can make -- find out about this. This seems to have -- it's dated the same as -- it has the same date as the previous document D977, and although it is definitely a different document, it bears the same reference number, that is 271/93. The second of these documents which are -- this will be marked as Defence Exhibit D978.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It seems to have the same reference number as D977. Then we have a second document which is being marked as document -- Defence document D979, it also consists of two pages, the English being the translation of the Serbo-Croat one. It's dated 13th of February, 1993, and it has ERN 04359210.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may offer a clarification. These are the Drina Corps archives documents, and we've encountered lots of cases such as this one. It is in a situation in which the commander, being the same person here, issues several orders under the same number at the same time, and you may encounter this yet. And it doesn't happen only with the Serb armed forces, but in some other documents as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I know. This is why I have --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is why I have mentioned it, because in fact we have encountered it in the past. It's two minutes before we are due to break. Should we break now?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This would be a good time for a break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We'll have a break of 30 minutes, resuming at quarter past 6.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is everything sorted out, Mr. Jones?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, I don't want to jinx things by saying definitely yes. Let's say "inch' Allah" he'll -- he'll be here as planned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because when I didn't see you return by the break, I said, we have problems. All right. Let's continue with this witness, please, Ms. Vidovic. How do you think you're doing?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, unfortunately we lost quite a lot of time on this particular discussion. I'm not sure we're making a lot of progress, but I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's go. Let's go ahead. Next question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you told us that you were not in the Kravica area during these subsequent attacks in mid-February 1993. Can you tell us where you were in the second half of January and the first half of February of 1993?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can tell you. I was in the area of Peciste, Djogazi, Likari, and Zanik.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know Naser Oric's whereabouts at the time? Did you see him?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was in Potocari and along the Budak-Dugo Polje line.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see him there often?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, every day.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did -- was Oric to be found in Srebrenica itself in the first -- in the second half of January and the first half of February of 1993 or was he, in fact, to be found at Potocari and the lines that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in fact in Potocari along the Budak-Dugo Polje line.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were one of the leaders of the groups in Potocari at the time. Were you aware of what was going on in the town of Srebrenica at the time?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because there was -- we were faced with such fierce artillery and infantry attacks that we did not have a moment to spare.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was Naser in the very same situation that you were?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at Dugo Polje and Budak.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your opinion was Naser able to follow what was happening in Srebrenica from the lines that he was holding?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was unable to.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he was exposed to strong artillery attacks from the direction of Bratunac and Sase.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could the witness be given a new document, please. This is a document by the command of the Bratunac Brigade number 04363130 dated 25 February 1993, which is a regular combat report addressed to the command of the Drina Corps. And I will quote item 2 of the document, which says: "Our forces fortified the lines reached and made preparations for the forthcoming operations. Since 1015 hours we have been firing our artillery in order to disturb and neutralise the enemy in the following sectors: Kamenica village - southern part, Srebrenica, Joseva, Gradac, Potocari, Pecista, Caus, Halilovici, and Vladusici." Do you remember the events around 25th February 1993.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because this was the time of the fiercest attacks. First there were artillery and air attacks followed by infantry attacks from the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does this document confirm this do you think?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the document be assigned an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic, this document will become D980. It has ERN 04 -- 04363130. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It true or not that in this period around the 25th of February, 1993, many Muslims villages fell?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at a different document now, which is a combat report by -- or rather, a regular combat report by the Bratunac Brigade command, bearing the following number: 04363132, dated 26th February 1993 addressed to the command of the Drina Corps. I will quote a portion thereof which says: "Our forces." And I will read the sentence starting in third line of item 2: "Pirici and Lemesac villages were attacked by a tank each. The brigade artillery group fired at specific targets in Srebrenica, Potocari, Kilavac, Sarampov, Siljkovici, and Halilovici, in order to disturb the enemy and inflict losses on them." A bit below lines are mentioned. And among other things it said "the enemy forces are among the following line: Potocari, Budak, Bljeceva. Do you recall where you were on the 26th of February, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. I was in the area of Djogazi, to be precise in the concrete manufacturing factory which was along the Bratunac-Srebrenica road.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What were you doing there? What was your business there?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went over there to lend a hand to the fighters in Djogazi who were expecting an imminent infantry attack, as they had just been exposed to a strong artillery attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was there a tank active in the area firing upon you?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this document be assigned a number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, this document will become Defence Exhibit D981.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was there anyone else in your close proximity?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To my left, across -- from the road in the area of Dugo Polje there was a group from Potocari, and among them was Naser.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why were they there, precisely?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just indicated a moment ago they were there because of a very strong artillery attack which always was premonitory of a strong infantry attack and this was at the very entrance to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We are now discussing the 26th of February, 1993. Are you quite certain that Naser Oric was in your immediate vicinity on that day?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm quite sure. I can confirm this -- not just I but another hundred people who were there close to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If someone were to claim that on the 26th of February, 1993, Naser Oric was at an exchange involving some Serb prisoners in Vitez in -- close to an area called Jezero, would that be true?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that would not be true for several reasons. The area where we were is 40 kilometres away from the site where the exchange took place. Secondly, the road from Potocari to Srebrenica was already under the control of the Serb forces from Causa and Zvijezda. They held it under very strong artillery fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you in fact aware of this exchange which took place on the 26th of February, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How did you come to know this? Can you tell that to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After demilitarisation I met with my friend Ramo Hljebara, who told me that in February -- or rather, on this particular date he had driven some Serb prisoners to Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did he tell you? Who were these people exchanged for?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These people were exchanged for our dead who were left behind in the villages that fell along the axis.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you anything of his role in this particular event?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was the driver of a truck -- or, rather, it was a TAM truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you who effected the exchange?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me that he drove Hamdija Fejzic, the president of the Executive Board of the War Presidency; Mirsad Dudic, who was also a member of the Presidency, because his brother stayed behind on the Serb territory; and Edhem, who was a cameraman there for the War Presidency, and I believe he filmed it all.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Edhem Vranjkovina therefore is the cameraman?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, who was attached to the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Perhaps he can tell us where he picked up these gentlemen from and also the persons that were exchanged, where they were coming from.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to hear from Ramo Hljebara more of the exchange, who the persons exchanged were, and where the exchange took place?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not tell me that. He did not tell me what their names were and how this came about; he just told me that he drove them over to Vitez with the people I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can I just ask you this: Is it true that Ramo Hljebara is still alive?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If someone were to claim that the vehicle was driven by Zulfo Tursunovic on this particular occasion, would that be true?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this man is half literate; secondly, he never possessed a driver's license or a vehicle -- or drove a vehicle. I remember that seeing him as a child, being at the head of a horse-drawn cart. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'll ask you something different now. The pressure put to bear by the Serb forces on Srebrenica and Potocari, did it continue in -- through to March 1993?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of March 1993, were you yourself in the vicinity of Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the time when the battles were at their fiercest in the vicinity of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the name of the locality?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We need you to repeat the name of the locality because the interpreters didn't catch it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which place was that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area of Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember anything that had to do with Naser Oric and was related to the 15th of March, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On that day there were fierce tank attacks launched. At one point a tank shell landed in our midst. I heard moans and I turned around and saw Naser helping there. At that point, Suljo ran up to him, Suljo Cakanovic [phoen], and tore his shoe apart and saw that his Achilles' heel had a large gaping wound.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that Naser was shouting and moaning?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was shouting at the top of his head. Suljo was dressing his wound, and Naser turned around all frightened asking whether his foot was going to be cut off. Suljo, putting a serious face on, said: No, no, there's no need for it to be cut off; it will fall off on its own.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, Naser Oric was wounded; he received a blow to the Achilles' heel on the 15th of March, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When did you see him next?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A couple of days later with one of my fighters. I went to see him in Potocari -- I went to fetch him, rather. I mounted him on a horse. His wound was in a terrible state.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you take him to a meeting, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was a meeting with Morillon, and I believe the venue of the meeting was at the post office.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was Naser able to move on his own or was he lame?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was not able to stand on his feet. His foot was swollen and his wound was oozing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If someone were to claim that Naser Oric drove a vehicle at this point in time or in the period of the ten following days, would that have been possible?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, for two reasons, the first one being that his wound was in terrible state; and the second, the fact that this particular stretch of roadway that I mentioned earlier was under enemy control.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I refer you to D220, Your Honours, which has to do with Naser Oric's infliction of his wound, and this is a document originating from the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I have the following question for you now: You, the Muslim people, including fighters, were you aware of an imminent tragedy resulting from the Serbs possibly entering Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was Oric aware of this?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was this a source of concern to him?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will show you two documents dating from the period.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will do my best to proceed as fast as I can. First of all, can the witness be shown a document bearing the numbers -- rather, two documents bearing the following numbers 04267588 and 04267584. They both bear the same date, and the source is the command of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, Witness, take a look at the document bearing the number 04267588, dated 17 March 1993. I will quote the last paragraph only. "On the 17th of March, 1993, therefore," the document says. From the command of the Drina Corps: "I have decided to use part of the forces to tighten the encirclement around Srebrenica and thus force the Muslims to surrender and use the remaining forces to fortify the lines reached, keep them at full combat readiness in order to prevent surprise, and incursion of enemy forces along all axes, and at the same time fortify the lines reached." I will now quote from the other document. Please look at the last page -- or rather, page 2 of the document. This is document dated 17 March 1993 signed by commander of the Drina Corps, Colonel Milenko Zivanovic. This portion reads: "I decided the following: To conduct combat activities with a part of forces towards Srebrenica in order to force civilian population to surrender, break, and destroy armed formations of the enemy in Srebrenica." In connection with these documents, I wish to ask you the following: Is it true that at the time on the 17th of March, 1993, the Serbs were tightening the circle around Srebrenica in an attempt to force the civilian Muslim population to surrender?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Based on your experience of the situation, did you have a feeling that Srebrenica was imminently being exposed to a catastrophe that was to follow in the next couple of days, that is after the 17th of March, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you were in contact with Oric. In this period from the 17th of March to the 22nd of March, 1993, were you in touch with Oric?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was he aware of the situation and was he very much concerned and did he do everything that was in his power to do, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was aware of the situation. When I went over to see him in Potocari, he was dejected, depressed, out of sorts, because he knew that he was unable to be of any assistance. He was lying bed-ridden, wounded. He appealed to us fighters and groups who were in the area to assist them and to stay at their side as long as we could.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could these documents be assigned a Defence exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. The first of these documents with ERN 04267588 to 589 is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D982. The other document with ERN 0467584 to 585 will become Defence Exhibit 983.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at another document now. This is a document by the Bratunac Brigade command dated 20 March 1993 which is a regular combat report addressed to the command of the Drina Corps. And while the document is being passed up, I will read a portion of it. "During the day our forces -- during the day along the main Bratunac-Potocari line, we conducted all preparations for an attack, but due to the arrival of Morillon and his escort, we gave up these activities." This attack, which purportedly was planned to take place on the 21st of March, 1993, did it in fact take place on the 21st of March or about that date, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on or about that date.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you in the area at the time?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was Naser Oric in Potocari at the time?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was in Potocari, wounded, in a house. He was unable to walk.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If someone were to claim that he was in Srebrenica on that day, would that be correct to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be assigned a number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This document with ERN 04363173 will become Defence Exhibit D984.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to have a video clip played now, which is part of Defence Exhibit D695, which is clip number 2 on this particular CD. Your Honour, I'm interested in what is being said and not in what we can see from the footage there. The source is Radio Television Bosnia and Herzegovina, Radio Tuzla. And could we please play the part from 00.01.32 to 00.02.19. I just want to say that we have the English version of the transcripts, and could we please listen to the transcript -- could we please distribute the transcript before we play the tape.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Just go safely and wisely and they will mess you about in the woods particularly because the woods are conifer woods and they are in those and not in the other ones. "Yes, yes. "Is that clear? "Clear. "Understood ... "We shot at Pribicevac ... "Right. Only shoot at live flesh, nothing else, only live flesh. Go around those hills of theirs, they have no weapons, no efficient weapons, they only have an odd Zolja, they have rifles, those simple ones. Everything from 300 metres go from the hill, cut off the road, there is neither water nor electricity on the hill. "Without food or anything they must run away. "Understood! "Just go deep. Do not cut into them. "Understand."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, have you recognised the voice?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the voice of Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to recognise the voice?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. The Bosnia-Herzegovina TV played footages of him repeatedly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And were you later on able to listen to his voice?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I was a member of the security forces, I had occasion to hear his voice.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the events which took place on the 17th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the time of very fierce battles in the area of Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And why did you happen to be there?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was our last resort, that's to say we had to save that area in order to save Srebrenica from falling.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: From the venue of Pribicevac, were you able to observe Zeleni Jadar or not?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were able to observe Zeleni Jadar because Zeleni Jadar is in a valley and Pribicevac is a hill.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the area of Zeleni Jadar, were there fighters trying to defend the area?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but very few. For the most part there were large groups of refugees there fleeing the Serb army. They were from the villages of Osmaci, Osata, Kragljivoda, Karadzici, and other hamlets.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your estimate in the area of Zeleni Jadar, how many civilians were there?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thousands.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear this person say "target the live flesh only"? What is your understanding of that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was able to hear. And my interpretation of it is to shoot at anything that moves, anything that is alive, so that it is destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know at the time that Ratko Mladic was in the area?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because he gave interviews. And I know the localities where he gave those interviews, in particular Zeleni Jadar, when I [Realtime transcript read in error "he"] went through the security agency material.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Based on the events in Zeleni Jadar at the time, did you know that the Serb command was close by?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was literally 1 to 200 metres away from Zeleni Jadar, looking from the area of Skelani and Podravanje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the recording, Ratko Mladic says "target only live flesh. Go around those villages of -- those hills of theirs. They have no weapons, just an odd Zolja and simple rifles." The information he conveyed, did it reflect the situation on the ground as to how many weapons you had?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the situation we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just a correction to the transcription. The preceding page, it's disappearing slowly, line 22. The witness said: "Yes, because he gave interviews. And I know the localities where he gave those interviews, in particular Zeleni Jadar." And then it says: "When he went through the security agency material." I heard this witness say: "When I went through the security agency material." This witness is saying "I went through it," not Mladic. That's what I understood. That's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I don't think it really makes sense, unless my -- what I heard is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I -- would you have a comment on what Mr. Di Fazio has just stated, please, Witness? Who went through the security agency material, you or someone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I personally went through the material.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you -- I would like to thank Mr. Di Fazio because the witness did not at any given moment say that Mladic did that. He said that he learned that Mladic was in Zeleni Jadar, having seen the interview, and not that he gave that interview in Zeleni Jadar itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Am I correct, Witness?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we please assign an exhibit number to the transcript because it hasn't been given one so that it be D695.1, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The tape itself or the video itself is -- has not yet been given a number yet, has it?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. It has been tendered as D695.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 695. And would you suggest that this be 695.1? So this document which is part of the transcript of the video would be D695.1. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I wanted to ask you something else. Did you ever meet Philipp von Recklinghausen?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who was he?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a photographer from Germany who came together with Senad Alic to Srebrenica. He took a number of photographs concerning the situation in Srebrenica, and later I learned that the Serbs took away the film from him.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know Senad Alic personally, even prior to the war?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. We grew up together in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When did Senad Alic come? You said that Mr. Philipp came with Senad Alic when was that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the end of February.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What year?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember where they came from?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Germany.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: From that point onwards, according to what you know, what was Senad Alic doing?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From that moment onwards, Senad Alic worked for the War Presidency as the liaison officer for the foreign journalists and UNPROFOR as well as an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did Senad Alic come together with Philip from Germany?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they came together.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why? What was he doing in Germany?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His parents lived in Germany. They had been living there since before the war for a while, and when the aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina came about, he went to Germany.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When he came to Srebrenica, did he wear a uniform and where did he get it from?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did, and he brought it with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As concerns Senad Alic, in your knowledge did he belong to any single armed group from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As I said a while ago, he was a personal interpreter to Fejzic and Amdic [as interpreted] with the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we show a photograph to the witness. The number is P460.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, did you receive the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A correction for the transcript, if I may, Fejzic and Avdic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Hajrudin.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look at the photograph. Please take a look at the photograph on the ELMO. Do you recognise anyone?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise Naser Oric, Hajrudin Malagic, second to the right; and Muharem, a.k.a. Suba, being the third person to the left.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the third person from the left.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Hajrudin Alagic [as interpreted] and Suba, were they in January in 1993 in the area of Srebrenica, according to what you know?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At the beginning of October, together with a group, they went to Tuzla. They stayed there until the end of February, and then -- then they came on board a UN helicopter.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who took this photograph?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It was Philipp.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If someone were to claim that this photograph was taken on the 7th of January, 1993, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wouldn't. Malagic, Hajrudin, and Suba were at that time in Tuzla. They came at the end of February, and this photograph could only have been taken in early March of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Smajlovic, I wanted to ask you an unrelated question, and it is concerning the fall of Srebrenica in 1995. Can you tell the Chamber when you left Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first half of January of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did your wife remain behind in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber what was happening with your wife on the day of the tragedy, that is the 11th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 11th of July, 1995, my wife gave birth in the battery factory. Since no one paid any attention to that, she found herself in a critical state, together with the infant. A UN member from the Dutch Battalion tried to help her so that she'd be put on a UN vehicle to catch up with the bus convoys that had already left with other women and children from the battery factory.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How far did this Dutch soldier manage to get together with your wife?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the village of Kravica. To be more precise, in front of the Oka, the agricultural cooperative. He was stopped by the military police, ordering him to go back. At that moment, a man approached the vehicle. He was cursing their mother and that he would kill both of them. And he ordered them back immediately.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did she -- did your wife see any of the -- of her relatives in the mass of people? Were there many people around Oka?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in front of the cooperative there were masses of civilians bare to the waist, together with the soldiers -- Serb soldiers with their weaponry aimed at them. And she recognised her brother, who had left for Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wonder if I have the time for another exhibit. It would take five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
